AI_GHOST_DEMAND.label: AI ghost demand
AI_GHOST_DEMAND.summary: The available evidence indicates that a significant portion of data‑center interconnection requests may be speculative or unfulfilled, a phenomenon described as “ghost demand.”  Multiple news reports (Reuters, Yahoo Finance, Investing.com) note that requests from large power users, mainly data centers, exceed 700 GW—more than ten times industry estimates of actual U.S. data‑center power use.  A Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities directive explicitly instructs electric distribution companies to eliminate speculative data‑center projects from interconnection queues, requiring lists of projects over 25 MW and data‑center projects over 1 MW.  These sources collectively support the claim that speculative interconnection requests are falling after deposit requirements are imposed, which is bearish for speculative developers but positive for suppliers with contracted backlog.  No official regulatory rule directly mandates deposit requirements, but the directive and the reported cancellations provide the necessary evidence for the mechanism.  No contradictory evidence was found in the candidate set.
